source.title: Weak and Strong Gradient Directions: Explaining Memorization, Generalization, and Hardness of Examples at Scale.
source.authors: Piotr Zieliński; Shankar Krishnan; Satrajit Chatterjee

record.tranche_reason: The study reports test-performance curves over training epochs on ImageNet, using label-noise conditions rather than a model-size sweep. These results bear on the epoch-wise version, but do not reproduce the original double-descent test.
record.gate_note: The study does not sweep model size or training-set sample size, and does not measure effective complexity. Its test-accuracy-over-epoch curves are relevant to V2. Results about suppressing weak gradients and easy/hard examples are not rows for the listed versions because they do not test a double-descent curve.
record.test_reason: The study tests the Coherent Gradients Hypothesis, not double descent. Its only double-descent link is citing Belkin et al. [4] in a list of generalization papers. The epoch-wise label-noise test curves (Fig 1a, 6a, 7a) are standard ImageNet runs of about 90 epochs with step or cosine learning-rate decay. The authors read them only as benign versus malignant overfitting. Neither the setup nor the analysis is aimed at whether a second descent occurs, and the short, decayed schedules could not show one. This is unlike the long, constant-rate training under which epoch-wise double descent was reported. So these curves do not test V2. The record's 'challenges' label overreaches.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude their results support the Coherent Gradients Hypothesis at scale. Suppressing weak gradient directions (M3/RM3) reduces overfitting and memorization, and easy examples generalize better among themselves than hard ones. Common patterns, rather than 'simple' ones, are learned first. They describe noisy-label test curves as malignant overfitting and never discuss double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines ImageNet training curves and label-noise effects, rather than sweeping model size, sample size, or effective complexity to test double descent.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-accuracy trajectory varies with label-noise condition: no-noise accuracy rises and stays flat, while noisy-label accuracy reaches a maximum and falls. The paper also reports results for ResNet-18, Inception-V3, and VGG-13.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet with ResNet-18, Inception-V3 and VGG-13, adding label noise makes test accuracy peak then fall within the training run. The fall grows with noise. At 0% noise, test accuracy rises then stays flat.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise turns benign overfitting (flat test accuracy) into malignant overfitting (falling test accuracy) during standard-length training, with the drop increasing with noise level.

record.problems: The relevant test-accuracy curves are presented in figures without numeric values or error bars. The study does not sweep model size or sample size, and does not characterize a second descent.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise relevant rows left out.

untested.parts: No long-horizon epoch-wise test-error curve examined for a second descent.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
Label noise is varied, but not in relation to a double-descent peak or to tuned regularization.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label for V2 should be dropped. The absence of a second descent within about 90 lr-decayed epochs (or early-stopped VGG runs) is not evidence against epoch-wise double descent. The authors did not look for one.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or interpolation-threshold measurement.
No test-error curve showing a second descent; the reported curves cover the tested training periods and conditions only.
No sweep over the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure or comparison of peak locations across axes.
Label noise is varied, but the study does not test whether double-descent peaks are driven by noise, split into multiple peaks, or disappear with optimally tuned regularization.
No comparison of the curve against an effective parameter count.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet with 0% randomized labels and plot test accuracy over epochs.
rows.locator: Figure 1(a); Section 2, Benign and Malignant Overfitting
rows.note: The text says test accuracy rises and then stays flat; this gives an initial improvement but not a fall-rise-fall curve.
rows.check: 0% noise control. The rise-then-flat test curve over about 90 epochs with lr decay cannot show or refute an epoch-wise second descent. Not a double-descent test.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet with 25% randomized labels and plot test accuracy over epochs.
rows.locator: Figure 1(a); Section 2, Benign and Malignant Overfitting
rows.note: The text says that with label noise, test accuracy reaches a maximum and then falls; it does not report a subsequent recovery.
rows.check: Peak-then-fall within about 90 epochs is reported as malignant overfitting. The training is too short and lr-decayed to show a recovery, and no later descent was sought.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: ResNet-18 on ImageNet, 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% label noise
reader_labels.reason: The reported curves show test accuracy rising then flattening without noise, and reaching a maximum then declining with label noise; no second improvement is reported, so the full fall-rise-fall pattern is not observed (r1-r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Inception-V3 and VGG-13 on ImageNet across the five label-noise settings
reader_labels.reason: The appendix curves are described as essentially the same as ResNet-18, but the text gives no separate verbal characterization of their epoch-wise test curves (r6-r15).
